summary: Visitors who need a Tanzanian visa can apply online, which Tanzania Immigration recommends, or obtain it on arrival: USD 50 for the ordinary single-entry visa, while US citizens must apply for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa. Nationals of the East African Community, of SADC countries except Comoros and of most Commonwealth countries do not need a visa, and the UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must also hold Tanzania's mandatory inbound travel insurance.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including those who spent more than 12 hours in transit at the airport of such a country.

source.name: WHO — Countries with risk of yellow fever transmission and countries requiring yellow fever vaccination

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: The Government of Canada says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas of Tanzania and at certain times of year, that antimalarial medication may be recommended depending on your itinerary and the time of year, and that you should consult a health professional, ideally six weeks before travel, and protect yourself from mosquito bites at all times.

source.name: Government of Canada — Tanzania travel advice (health)

travelInsurance.text: The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must hold Tanzanian mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought for their first port of entry: from the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) if they arrive in mainland Tanzania first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) if they arrive in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, it covers up to 92 days, other insurance is not accepted in its place, and it can be bought online or on arrival. Visitors without it may be refused entry.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Tanzania entry requirements

onwardTicket.text: Visitors must show their return ticket on arrival.

declarations.text: Foreign visitors who arrive in Zanzibar first must hold the inbound travel insurance issued by the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation; proof of other international insurance is not accepted. currencyLimits.text: The Government of Canada says all currencies exceeding USD 10,000 must be declared on arrival in and departure from Tanzania.

source.name: Government of Canada — Tanzania travel advice (money)

notes: The UK Foreign Office says plastic bags are banned: if you arrive by air you will be asked to hand them over, although zip-lock bags used for airline security are not included.
Canada's travel advice says you must obtain a permit from the Tanzania Civil Aviation Authority to import a drone.

The UK Foreign Office says exporting wildlife items, including horns and seashells, without a certified export permit from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism is illegal, and advises against bringing animal-skin accessories into the country.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office (FCDO) advises against all but essential travel to any area within 20 km of Tanzania's border with the Cabo Delgado province of Mozambique, because of attacks by groups linked with Islamic extremism. It also says tourists in Dar es Salaam have been 'express kidnapped', robbed and forced to withdraw cash from ATMs, and that it is safest to arrange a taxi through a hotel or travel operator.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says Tanzania requires mandatory inbound travel insurance, covering up to 92 days: from the National Insurance Corporation if you land on the mainland first, or from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44, according to its FAQ) if you land in Zanzibar first. One policy is enough, and your own insurance does not replace it.
US citizens cannot buy the USD 50 single-entry visa. They are only eligible for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa, valid 12 months.
Visas can also be obtained on arrival at official entry points, but Tanzania Immigration recommends applying online, and only through its official website, not through any other online links.
The UK Foreign Office says plastic bags are banned in Tanzania and air arrivals are asked to hand them over; zip-lock bags for airline security are not included in the ban.
Uganda's Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control says the East African Tourist Visa allows travel to Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda only. It is not valid for Tanzania, which needs its own visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Tanzania?
faq.answer: Nationals of the East African Community, of SADC countries except Comoros and of Commonwealth countries other than the United Kingdom, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand do not need a visa. Others need one: the ordinary single-entry visa costs USD 50, online or on arrival, while US citizens must apply for the USD 100 multiple-entry visa.

faq.question: Does the Tanzanian visa cover Zanzibar?
faq.answer: Yes. Tanzania's visa guidelines say a visitor to both the mainland and Zanzibar selects the first destination on the form and may visit both without a new visa. The UK Foreign Office says all visitors except residents must also hold the mandatory inbound travel insurance, bought once for the first port of entry: from the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (USD 44) if you arrive in Zanzibar first, or from the National Insurance Corporation if you arrive on the mainland first.

faq.question: Can I get a Tanzanian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: For the nationalities on the guidelines' visa-on-arrival list, yes, at official entry points. Nationals of the 23 countries on the guidelines' no-visa-on-arrival list (among them Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Iran, Pakistan, Somalia and Syria), stateless people and refugees cannot, unless the Commissioner General of Immigration has given special permission: they must hold an approved eVisa before travelling. Tanzania Immigration recommends applying online.

faq.question: Why do US citizens pay more for a Tanzanian visa?
faq.answer: Tanzania's visa guidelines say that, under bilateral agreements between Tanzania and the United States, US passport holders are not entitled to the ordinary visa and must apply for the multiple-entry visa (USD 100, valid up to 12 months) even for a single trip.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Tanzania?
faq.answer: Only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from, or spent more than 12 hours in transit at the airport of, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

faq.question: Is the East Africa Tourist Visa valid for Tanzania?
faq.answer: No — despite the name, Uganda's Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control says the East African Tourist Visa allows travel to Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda only. Tanzania requires its own visa or visa exemption.
